name: Waxahatchee
label: Anti-
lede: Katie Crutchfield named a cassette after a creek near her Alabama home, and twelve years later Pitchfork ranked her sixth album No. 6 of 2024.

eras.title: Twins on the Alabama circuit
eras.text: Katie and Allison Crutchfield play out as teenagers in Alabama and never really stop. By 2011 they've been through two bands, and Katie is ready to go alone.

years.h: Alabama twins Katie and Allison Crutchfield start the Ackleys
years.p: Born January 4, 1989, they put out a self-titled album and the EP Forget Forget, Derive Derive.
years.xp: By 17, Katie was playing Cave9, a Birmingham all-ages room, nearly every week, according to Grantland's 2015 profile.

years.h: Katie Crutchfield writes every P.S. Eliot song
years.p: After the Ackleys, the sisters restart as [[P.S. Eliot|97017fae-cdcd-47f1-843d-4a69a81675ed]] with Will Granger and Katherine Simonetti, tour the US on a DIY circuit and release on Salinas Records.
years.xp: P.S. Eliot made Introverted Romance in Our Troubled Minds (2009, Salinas), the Living in Squalor EP (2010, Freedom School) and Sadie (2011, Salinas). Katie later told an interviewer she drove every decision in the band, including writing all the songs.

years.cap: Allison Crutchfield and Keith Spencer with Swearin', Sweat It Fest, Rock Hill, South Carolina
years.h: P.S. Eliot play their last show at Death By Audio in Brooklyn
years.p: After four years, with members in different cities and wanting different music, the band calls it.
years.xp: Allison had already moved to Philadelphia, where she started [[Swearin'|5b62be91-b158-40a7-a51d-43b1a3b91ec3]] with Kyle Gilbride, Keith Spencer and Jeff Bolt. Katie went the other way, back to Alabama, and kept writing.

eras.title: A cassette gets a band
eras.text: Katie Crutchfield records on cassette, signs to Don Giovanni, and by the second album has a band, borrowed from her sister's.

years.h: A creek gives Katie Crutchfield's solo project its name
years.p: Her first solo songs come out on cassette while P.S. Eliot is still active, under the name of Waxahatchee Creek, near where she grew up in Alabama.

years.h: American Weekend is written and recorded in about a week
years.p: Don Giovanni releases the debut Katie Crutchfield made at her family's home in Birmingham.
years.xp:
Grantland's account has the songs coming over seven winter days after a breakup, and Wikipedia says it was recorded in a week at her family's house. NPR picked "Be Good" as a Song of the Day in June 2012 and later put it among its 50 favorite songs of the year.

The Times and Dusted both named it a top album of 2012. Paste placed it No. 238 on its 2025 list of the best albums of the century so far.

years.big: "Skilled enough to make introspection not self-centered, but generous."
years.h: Cerulean Salt arrives with a band and Pitchfork's Best New Music
years.p: Pitchfork's Lindsay Zoladz on the record Katie Crutchfield made in a West Philadelphia basement with Allison, Kyle Gilbride, Keith Spencer and Sam Cook-Parrott.
years.xp: Recorded September to November 2012 and released March 5, 2013 on Don Giovanni in the US and Wichita in the UK. Pitchfork gave it 8.4 with Best New Music and ranked it No. 22 of 2013.

years.h: Waxahatchee supports Tegan and Sara in the UK
years.p: A headline run follows in October, and Cerulean Salt reaches No. 1 on the Official Record Store Chart in July.

eras.title: The loud years on Merge
eras.text: A bigger label, a bigger sound, and a record about what the touring was doing to her. Katie trades the four-track for a band and a proper studio.

years.cap: Katie Crutchfield solo at Fletcher Opera Theater, Raleigh, North Carolina, September 2015
years.h: Ivy Tripp: a year in Holbrook, Long Island, and a new label
years.p: Katie Crutchfield leaves Don Giovanni for Merge and spends nearly a year in a Holbrook house co-producing with Keith Spencer.
years.xp:
"Best day of my life," Crutchfield told Grantland of signing to Merge, a day spent hanging out and getting drunk with the band. She also said songs that once took an hour now take months.

The album hit No. 15 on the US Indie chart. Pitchfork gave it 8.1, and Rolling Stone put it at No. 15 of 2015.

years.cap: Waxahatchee at the Neptune Theatre, Seattle, July 2017
years.h: Out in the Storm is a breakup record with a rhythm section
years.p: Recorded live at Miner Street in Philadelphia with John Agnello, who has worked with Dinosaur Jr. and Sonic Youth, and a full band including Allison Crutchfield on keyboards.
years.xp: The band: Allison Crutchfield, Katie Harkin, Katherine Simonetti on bass and Ashley Arnwine on drums. The album peaked at No. 7 on the US Indie chart. Pitchfork gave it 8.2 and ranked it No. 13 on its Best Rock Albums list of 2017.

years.h: Waxahatchee opens for Jawbreaker at Brooklyn Steel
years.p: She also supports Jawbreaker at the Hollywood Palladium on March 10, the band's first Los Angeles shows in 22 years.

years.cap: Katie Crutchfield at Traveler's Rest, Missoula, Montana, August 2018
years.h: The low point at Primavera Sound ends her drinking
years.p: Katie Crutchfield has said she hit bottom at Barcelona's Primavera Sound, and the turn became "Oxbow", the opening song on Saint Cloud.
years.xp: She was 29 when she got sober. She told Grammy.com in 2024 that drinking "had a weight to it that it didn't have for everyone I knew." She also told Billboard in 2020 that Saint Cloud was largely about stopping.

years.h: A Great Thunder EP fills the gap between albums
years.p: Merge puts it out in September 2018; it reaches No. 26 on the US Indie chart and No. 6 on Heatseekers.

eras.title: Sober, and sounding like it
eras.text: A quieter record, a country turn, and a pandemic that puts her songs in a lot of headphones. Recording moves to Texas and New York with a new producer, Brad Cook.

years.cap: Katie Crutchfield at Huichica, Walla Walla, Washington
years.h: Saint Cloud arrives as lockdown begins
years.p: Recorded in summer 2019 at Sonic Ranch in Texas and Long Pond in New York, the first Waxahatchee album with Brad Cook producing.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and ranked it No. 2 of 2020, the same spot Paste gave it. Rolling Stone put it No. 7, and it won Best Country Record at the 2021 Libera Awards.

Lead single "Fire" arrived in January. Crutchfield called it an anthem for self-acceptance.

years.cap: Katie Crutchfield with an acoustic guitar
years.h: With tours cancelled, Waxahatchee plays whole albums from home
years.p: Katie Crutchfield runs a livestream series, each show covering one record.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the series as a deep dive into her back catalog, meant to reach her fans and bring in some income while touring was off.

years.h: "Lilacs" gets a video and a spot on adult alternative radio
years.p: The video comes out February 18, 2020, and the song charts on the AAA format, No. 26 on one list.

years.h: Crutchfield writes the soundtrack for Apple TV+'s El Deafo
years.p: The kids' series soundtrack comes out January 7, 2022 on Apple Video Programming and Merge.

years.big: "The big pivotal moment for me and Brad."
years.h: Brad Cook flies [[MJ Lenderman|4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc]] to Sonic Ranch
years.p: Katie Crutchfield on the harmonies she and Lenderman sing on "Right Back to It" at the sessions.
years.xp: Cook arranged for Lenderman, whom Crutchfield had met at SXSW, to come to Sonic Ranch in August 2022. His harmonies on the demo changed what the song became.

years.h: Katie Crutchfield and Jess Williamson record as Plains
years.p: They met through Kevin Morby in 2017, wrote separately through lockdown and release I Walked with You a Ways on Anti-, with [[MJ Lenderman|4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc]] on the tour.
years.xp: Plains was billed as a one-off. The record draws on 1990s pop-country and classic country.

eras.title: The year of Tigers Blood
eras.text: Crutchfield and Cook return to Sonic Ranch, add MJ Lenderman on guitar and make the record critics rank all year.

yt: Right Back to It (feat. MJ Lenderman)
years.h: A rowboat on Caddo Lake carries "Right Back to It"
years.p: Katie Crutchfield and MJ Lenderman sing in a rowboat in the video for the lead single, an idea she'd had for over a decade.
years.xp:
Her team had called the idea a logistical nightmare. It was inspired by the Lemonheads' "Mrs. Robinson" video. The song was recorded at Sonic Ranch in August 2022 and debuted at No. 39 on Billboard's Adult Alternative Airplay chart.

Pitchfork named it Best New Track and ranked it No. 2 of its 100 best songs of 2024. The pair played it on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert in March 2024.

years.cap: Waxahatchee onstage at the Sydney Opera House, December 2024
years.h: Tigers Blood lands at No. 6 on Pitchfork's 2024 list
years.p: Anti- releases the record; Pitchfork gave it 8.8 and Best New Music before the year-end ranking.
years.xp:
Brad Cook produced at Sonic Ranch. Lenderman played electric guitar throughout, Phil Cook handled banjo, Dobro and organ, and Spencer Tweedy played drums. Metacritic landed at 89. Consequence and Exclaim! both put it No. 3 of the year; Uncut had it No. 10.

Crutchfield told Grammy.com she wrote the songs over about six months, many of the lyrics on the road, and chose to "depend solely on the songs" rather than reinvent the sound.

years.h: She plays 2,500-seat theaters and passes on bigger rooms
years.p: Katie Crutchfield keeps the North American tour intimate, from April to August.

years.h: Rolling Stone reports her first Grammy nomination
years.p: Tigers Blood is up for Best Americana Album, after more than a decade of records.

eras.title: Sisters again
eras.text: The twins make a record together, Crutchfield sings on other people's songs, and Waxahatchee keeps going.

years.h: The Crutchfield sisters surprise-release Snocaps
years.p: A teaser leads to an Anti- album with both sharing lead vocals, MJ Lenderman on multiple instruments and Brad Cook producing.

years.h: Crutchfield sings on Courtney Barnett's "Site Unseen"
years.p: Barnett says of Katie, "I really love Katie's songwriting and her voice."
